key_insight: UniSlider makes image-editing sliders feel natural by aligning slider movement with perceptual change, not just raw model strength. This produces smoother, more intuitive control with fewer dead zones and sudden jumps.
problem_solved: Current generative image-editing sliders usually control internal strength parameters directly, but those parameters do not map well to what users actually see. As a result, slider motion can cause no visible change for long ranges, abrupt transformations in short ranges, or even partial reversals.
method: Remap the underlying model strength to a perceptually uniform slider scale.
Calibrate the slider so equal movements correspond to more consistent visual changes across the editing range.
Improve continuous image editing interfaces for generative methods that use adapter weights, prompt weights, or interpolation factors.
impact: For AI/ML practitioners, UniSlider enables more reliable and user-friendly control over generative edits. It can improve interactive workflows in image editing tools by making parameter tuning more predictable and interpretable.

paper_title: UniSlider: Perceptually Uniform Sliders for Continuous Image Editing
paper_authors: David Serrano-Lozano, Duygu Ceylan, Yannick Hold-Geoffroy, Iliyan Georgiev, Javier Vazquez-Corral
